The minimum number of elements that must be added to the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo></math> so that it is a symmetric relation, is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi></math>

solution.text:
Given,

Set A=10,9,8,7,6,4,3,0

Now relation x-y is odd or x-y=2 can be given by,

R=(10,9),(10,8),(10,7),(10,3),(9,8),(9,7),(9,6),(9,4),(9,0),(8,7),(8,6),(8,3),(7,6),(7,4),(7,0),(6,4),(6,3),(4,3),(3,0)

So, total there are 19 elements and all the elements of R, (a, b) are of type a > b.

Hence, we need to add total of 19 more elements to R to make in symmetric
